mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate) of investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public certification, then Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) certification, then Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification for mainland use; this is the consular-legalization-equivalent cross-strait route and is mutually exclusive with Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention Contracting Party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public certifies a true copy, SEF certifies the notarial act, and ARATS verifies the SEF certification; this is a consular-legalization-equivalent path, parallel to and never combined with Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney (Appointing Incorporation Agent and Bank Signatories)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and Shareholders of the Taiwan investing company; signature certified by a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public, followed by SEF certification and ARATS verification; this consular-legalization-equivalent route is used exclusively because Taiwan cannot issue a Hague Apostille recognized by mainland authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (registered articles) or notarized copy of the registered articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registered articles are copied and notarized by a Taiwan notary public, then SEF-certified and ARATS-verified; no Hague Apostille is available for Taiwan-origin documents, so the cross-strait consular-legalization-equivalent process applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank in Taiwan, issued on official bank letterhead and signed by the branch manager or compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank signature is notarized by a Taiwan notary public, followed by SEF certification and ARATS verification; this is a standalone consular-legalization-equivalent authentication path and must never be chained with Hague Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The WFOE and its Taiwan investor must screen all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the PRC domestic restricted lists, the Supreme People's Court dishonest judgment debtor list, CSRC market prohibition lists, SAMR blacklists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, and World Bank debarment list. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth documentation, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring. Screening must be refreshed every 90 days, immediately upon any change in ownership or adverse media, and all records must be preserved for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Registration and Examination System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE's statutory name must be composed exclusively of simplified Chinese characters in the four-tier structure: administrative division name + distinctive trade name + industry description + organizational form. English or pinyin names are supplementary and not registrable as the legal name; an unrelated English trademark may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese characters before submission.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 1, 2, 4, 8, 18, 98-113, 128-130, 156, 207, 387; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 1, 4, 7, 8; Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan from the Mainland Area, Articles 2, 4 and 6.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division, Taiwan, R.O.C.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for Incorporation (Application for Registration of a Limited Company), together with the certified Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Taiwan Company Act; however, the subscribed paid-in capital must be reasonably sufficient to cover formation and initial operating costs, must be remitted into a Taiwan bank account opened in the proposed company name, and must remain deposited until the company registration certificate is issued. For a Mainland China-invested applicant, the Investment Commission may impose capital amount or source-of-funds conditions through the investment permission letter. No blocked escrow account is otherwise required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: For the mainland China WFOE: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic compliance is performed through the STA's National Electronic Tax Bureau online tax service platform and the provincial electronic tax bureaus. For any Taiwan-side tax filing obligation of the Taiwan parent: Ministry of Finance of Taiwan, acting through the National Taxation Administration and the local national tax bureaus, including the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Mainland China WFOE: (1) complete incorporation registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation or the competent local Market Supervision Administration; (2) obtain the business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code, which is the statutory taxpayer identification number for Chinese tax purposes and is automatically shared with the STA; (3) complete the consolidated tax registration at the competent local tax authority within 30 days of the business license issue date; (4) determine VAT taxpayer status, remaining a small-scale taxpayer below RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales or electing VAT general taxpayer status; (5) if exporting goods, register with the Customs Administration and obtain or update the customs declaration registration code. For a foreign or non-resident enterprise without a Chinese permanent establishment, such as the Taiwan parent, the non-resident enterprise must file Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Registration with the competent STA and obtain a non-resident tax identification number to support Chinese withholding obligations; the Taiwan parent does not receive a Chinese Unified Social Credit Code unless it establishes a branch or subsidiary in mainland China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The CN WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China and is subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income at the entity level. It is not a pass-through entity, and distributions to the Taiwan shareholder remain subject to Chinese dividend withholding tax where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for pass-through or check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections in China include the VAT small-scale taxpayer versus general taxpayer election, with general taxpayer status becoming mandatory above RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales, and accounting-method elections under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available in mainland China; the Taiwan parent remains governed by Chinese non-resident withholding rules and Taiwan domestic tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (VAT), with a 13% headline rate for goods, 9% for certain designated goods and services, and 6% for modern services, including information technology, software, software-as-a-service, and helpdesk cloud services. Export goods and qualifying cross-border services are zero-rated. Taiwan levies Business Tax on goods and services in Taiwan, generally at 5%, including reverse-charge on imported services where the Taiwan customer is a registered business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary threshold for obtaining the Unified Social Credit Code-based tax identity; every mainland China enterprise must complete tax registration. The VAT general taxpayer registration threshold is RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales. Below this threshold, the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer and may enjoy the prevailing small-scale taxpayer monthly exemption, currently capped at RMB 100,000 in taxable sales per month, or may elect general taxpayer status. Exceeding RMB 5,000,000 makes general taxpayer registration mandatory. For Taiwan, a mainland WFOE supplying services to Taiwan has no Taiwan VAT registration obligation solely by reason of export supplies; Taiwan VAT or Business Tax is generally collected by reverse-charge on the Taiwan business customer, unless the WFOE establishes a Taiwan fixed place of business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China: fully digitalized electronic invoices, known as shu dian piao, are issued through the National Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform administered by the STA. Invoice numbers are allocated in real time, invoice data is transmitted to the tax authority at issuance, and the digital electronic seal and anti-fraud controls are embedded in the invoice. Paper special VAT invoices must be issued through authorized tax-control equipment or tax disk where a counterparty still requires paper-format invoices. Taiwan: domestic Taiwan sellers must transmit cloud-based electronic invoices to the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform in near-real time; a foreign exporter without a Taiwan fixed place of business is not required to issue Taiwan electronic invoices for exports of services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: China zero-rates export goods and qualifying cross-border services, including software services, information system services, business process management services, and remote helpdesk or customer-support cloud services, where the service recipient is outside mainland China and the service is consumed entirely outside mainland China. For this WFOE, the omni-channel helpdesk and conversational-bot cloud services supplied to Taiwan customers may be zero-rated if the contract, payment evidence, service delivery logs, and place-of-consumption indicators demonstrate that the service is performed and used outside mainland China. The statutory basis includes the VAT interim regulations and the value-added tax reform framework under Caishui [2016] No. 36, together with the STA cross-border taxable services administration measures. If physical goods are sold alongside the cloud service, the goods must be properly exported through customs to support zero-rating for the goods element.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration and the corresponding electronic customs data from the China Electronic Port single-window system where physical goods are exported
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill where physical goods are exported
Commercial contract or framework agreement with the Taiwan customer identifying the service recipient, scope of services, place of consumption, and payment terms
Zero-rated VAT sales invoice, issued as a fully digitalized electronic invoice or special VAT invoice where required
Inward Remittance Certificate, Foreign Currency Collection Certificate, or bank confirmation of cross-border foreign exchange repatriation from the Taiwan customer
Cross-border payment gateway settlement reports from Stripe Billing or PayPal showing gross receipts, fees, currency, and payee details

Service delivery and consumption evidence, including IP addresses, server logs, helpdesk ticket records, conversational-bot session logs, and cloud usage reports demonstrating that services are rendered and consumed outside mainland China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China: if the zero-rating claim is unsupported, false, or fraudulent, the STA will claw back any input VAT refund, reapply VAT at the applicable rate of 6% for information technology and software services, charge late-payment interest, and may impose administrative penalties from 50% up to five times the underpaid tax. Customs penalties may also apply where export declarations or supporting transport documents have been misused. The 180-day foreign exchange repatriation deadline may be extended only for genuine force majeure or documented administrative delay. Taiwan: a Taiwan business customer that fails to reverse-charge Taiwan Business Tax on imported services may be liable for tax surcharges and penalties under the Taiwan Business Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People’s Republic of China, operating under the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), for the mainland China WFOE; the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) governs the Taiwan parent-side settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible on current-account items, including service-trade proceeds from SaaS/helpdesk export revenue, but remains a regulated currency on capital-account items. A China WFOE with a Taiwan parent requires SAFE registration for each FDI equity injection; the injected RMB must be used within the approved business scope and cannot be arbitrarily converted into off-balance-sheet or speculative instruments. Profit remittance by the WFOE to Taiwan is treated as a current-account remittance but is subject to a combination of tax clearance certificates, audited financial statements, and bank documentary review. In practice, the bank will require the annual SAFE foreign-exchange business report and proof of dividends. Because the NTD and RMB cross-strait settlement regimes require special settlement arrangements, the Taiwan parent may receive RMB through Taipei/Shanghai clearing bank lines, but onshore capital movement remains under PBOC/SAFE oversight. Surrender requirements have been liberalised: current-account foreign-exchange receipts may be retained or voluntarily settled, but all proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic SAFE-regulated account within the statutory period. Overall, no full capital-account convertibility exists, and all treasury operations must be pre-mapped to SAFE codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: 100 percent of export service and goods proceeds must be repatriated to a SAFE-designated domestic foreign-exchange account within 180 days from the date of invoice or service completion; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0 percent because the compulsory surrender regime has been abolished, but an enterprise may elect to convert any portion to RMB; retained foreign-exchange balances are subject to the SAFE-approved current-account balance cap, and non-repatriation triggers SAFE administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not viable as the primary treasury rails for the mainland China WFOE. SAFE and PBOC regulations require all foreign-exchange transactions of a PRC company to be settled through a licensed domestic bank or a SAFE-approved licensed payment institution. Global EMIs cannot issue a domestic RMB clearing account, perform SAFE reporting, or act as a statutory counterparty for capital-account flows. For the target rails Stripe_Billing and PayPal, PayPal may only be used to collect offshore card payments if the WFOE works through a licensed cross-border payment service provider or a foreign acquiring entity before routing funds via SWIFT MT103 through the domestic bank; Stripe does not maintain a licensed PRC onshore receiving entity for a WFOE. An offshore treasury vehicle such as a Hong Kong company may hold Stripe/PayPal balances, but the WFOE’s statutory books, SAFE FDI registration, and domestic tax filings require funds to be repatriated through the licensed banking channel. Therefore the feasibility rating is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the FDI capital-account opening, the statutory legal representative must appear physically at the mainland China branch for a face-to-face KYC interview and sign the account-opening pack; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by most Tier-1 banks for a capital account. For the RMB current operating account, some banks accept a remote video interview for a Taiwan-resident legal representative, but still require an authentic power of attorney, original passport or Taiwan Compatriot Permit, and physical on-site identity verification of the authorized person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwanese shareholder chain exceeding three tiers with bearer or unnamed holding vehicles, and a non-resident UBO without a PRC tax identification number.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly authenticated Taiwan corporate registry extract, signed group structure chart by the UBO, two years of audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent, passport and Taiwan Compatriot Permit, PRC Individual Tax filing or UBO declaration under PBOC Decree No. 3, and bank reference letters from the Taiwan funding bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction purpose code mismatch where the incoming equity capital remittance is classified as ordinary service payment due to missing SAFE FDI registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign-Invested Enterprise Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate, FDI business registration information from the State Administration for Market Regulation, board resolution approving the equity injection, and a destination-of-funds memo for the Helpdesk SaaS platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or negative-media detection on the Taiwanese parent shareholder, especially where the parent has government or military connections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions screening results from OFAC, UN, EU and PRC lists, negative-news diligence dossier, PEP self-declaration, notarized CV of the beneficial shareholder, and audited financial statements proving the legitimate source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained mismatch between the declared software/helpdesk business scope and payment flows to high-risk jurisdictions or unusual counterparty patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer contracts, commercial invoices, service-level agreements, payment-processor reconciliation reports from Stripe and PayPal, IP and cloud-hosting agreements, and a phase-wise projected transaction profile for the Helpdesk business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires the Taiwan parent to pass a board resolution, the WFOE to complete SAFE FDI registration and obtain the FDI registration certificate, and the Taiwan parent to remit via SWIFT MT103 directly to the WFOE FDI capital account at a Tier-1 domestic bank using the direct investment equity capital purpose code with the SAFE registration number referenced in the payment details. After receipt, a PRC-licensed CPA performs capital verification, and funds are credited to the capital account and may be converted to RMB for permitted operating expenses; third-party remitters, split remittances designed to avoid SAFE reporting, and cash injections are prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For SaaS and helpdesk service disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 with the service-trade purpose code and supporting contract, invoice, and tax payment certificate. For any subordinate physical goods trade, use a commercial letter of credit (MT700) or documentary collection when cross-border title transfer occurs. All current-account payments must be submitted to the designated bank with a complete transaction archive retained for at least five years; unlicensed EMI or P2P settlement rails are not permitted onshore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward sale and purchase contracts concluded with the Tier-1 domestic bank after providing genuine trade background and SAFE real-demand documentation; no speculative positions are permitted.
Onshore FX swaps and currency options with PBOC/SAFE-approved counterparties, limited to the notional amount of the WFOE’s known current-account or approved capital-account exposure.

Offshore NDFs or offshore RMB forwards are not permissible for the onshore WFOE; the Taiwan parent may use offshore NDF markets to hedge Taiwan-side investment currency risk, but the WFOE itself cannot take an offshore NDF position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual written shareholder consent approving the business report, financial statements, and profit distribution or loss-covering proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs — records maintained for on-demand inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where the company fails to obtain shareholder approval within the statutory deadline, MOEA may order rectification and impose an administrative fine of TWD 20,000 to TWD 1,000,000 (approximately USD 645 to USD 32,258 at 31 TWD/USD); repeated non-compliance or prolonged dormant operation may trigger administrative dissolution or strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CPA-audited and certified financial statements filed with the company registration authority (required when the statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; official due date is 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file certified financial statements when legally required exposes the company to a warning, an administrative fine of TWD 20,000 to TWD 1,000,000, and, in cases of sustained non-compliance with no business operation, administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise annual income tax return (business income tax return) including audited statements where turnover exceeds the certification threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), local National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing season from 1 May to 31 May following the calendar year-end; extensions apply only on formal application to the tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax for each additional two-month delinquency window, subject to a minimum penalty of TWD 15,000; unpaid tax accrues daily interest; failure to file allows the tax authority to make an official assessment with additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employee tax withholding and earnings statements filed for prior-year salary and remuneration payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), local National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar year in which income was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-reporting of withholding statements may result in a per-statement penalty under the Tax Collection Act, an administrative fine, and in cases of deliberate omission, criminal or aggravated monetary sanctions; continued failure to file can also impede corporate certification and tax clearance applications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Major shareholder and beneficial ownership register update with the MOEA corporate information platform (required only when a shareholding or control change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration and Beneficial Ownership Information Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any shareholding transfer, beneficial ownership change, director or manager change, or change in percentage of shares held by a major shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the statutory beneficial ownership reporting duty is subject to administrative fines of TWD 20,000 to TWD 1,000,000 for the company and responsible officer; persistent default may constitute a formalized breach affecting company status and voluntary strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment compliance update for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise (where foreign shareholding is registered with the investment authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any approved shareholding change or capital alteration; an annual internal reconciliation is required before the shareholder approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report foreign investment changes may result in administrative warning, suspension of the investment approval, restriction of tax and remittance privileges, and potential forced administrative deregistration of the investment approval.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit is statutorily mandatory in Taiwan when: (a) the company has paid-in capital of TWD 30 million or more, approximately USD 967,742; or (b) annual sales or operating revenue reaches TWD 100 million or more, approximately USD 3,225,806, in which case the profit-seeking enterprise income tax return must be audited and certified by a CPA; or (c) the company operates in a regulated industry such as banking, insurance, securities, or a combined commercial and financial activity where special law mandates audit; or (d) the company is a branch or investee of a foreign enterprise whose parent requires IFRS/TFRS-audited group consolidation statements. There is no general employee headcount threshold under Taiwan Company Act that triggers a statutory audit; however, headcount-based obligations under labor pension, health insurance, and employment insurance laws remain independently applicable. Balance sheet and turnover thresholds are measured per the fiscal year before the filing obligation and are not waived for small or single-shareholder WFOE limited liability companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies in Taiwan prepare statutory financial statements in accordance with the Business Accounting Act and the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS), which are aligned with the IFRS-for-SMEs approach; public companies and foreign-invested enterprises with group reporting requirements may apply Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS) which are converged with IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. The applicable framework must be disclosed consistently and applied to the balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, and cash flow statement for the statutory audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a fixed annual UBO return similar to a UK-style confirmation statement; however, under Company Act Article 22-1, the company must maintain accurate major shareholder and beneficial ownership data and file any change to that data with the MOEA beneficial ownership platform within 30 days of the triggering event, including share transfers, director or manager changes, or changes in a natural person's shareholding crossing the 10% threshold. In addition, the WFOE must conduct an annual internal reconciliation of its statutory registers and UBO data before the shareholder written approval of financial statements; the reconciliation is evidenced by a board-level record and kept available for MOEA and Investment Commission inspection. Any foreign share transfer must also be approved or recorded with the MOEA Investment Commission where required by the foreign investment approval conditions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing shareholder written consents and board meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,000 per annum for a Taiwan registered office address and local corporate agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000 per annum for a CPA audit of a small-to-mid-sized wholly foreign-owned limited liability company preparing EAS/TFRS financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard PRC Enterprise Income Tax at 25%; reduced 15% rate for National High and New Technology Enterprises; 15% promoted-encouraged rates in Hainan Free Trade Port and Shanghai Lingang New Area; 20% reduced rate for small low-profit enterprises with effective tax burden of approximately 5% on qualifying annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; general 5-year loss carryforward, extended to 10 years for high- and new-technology enterprises and technology-oriented small and medium enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (with underlying schedule pack) and Quarterly Prepayment Return Form A200000; both filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax portal) at the WFOE's registration-place competent tax authority.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments due within 15 calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter; annual final return and payment due by May 31 of the immediately following calendar tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide revenue of the WFOE, including multi-channel helpdesk SaaS subscription fees, setup fees, storage/retention fees and customer-support packages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise subscription revenue under PRC tax and accounting rules; where services are rendered to non-resident customers, apply China-source service rules and arm's-length pricing with any Taiwan or offshore group entities; reconcile revenue-recognition timing differences between financial statements and the tax return in Schedule A105000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of producing helpdesk and conversational-bot services: cloud infrastructure, third-party chatbot APIs, staff costs of customer support engineers, and subcontractor charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharge invoices from the Taiwan parent or affiliates are deductible only if the services confer a real commercial benefit, are not duplicative, and comply with the arm's-length principle and contemporaneous documentation; unsupported or circular service fees must be adjusted as non-deductible expenditures and may be reclassified as deemed dividends subject to 10% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, property tax, land-use tax, stamp duty and other taxes directly related to business operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include PRC VAT or Enterprise Income Tax; input VAT not fully credit because of non-deductible or personal-use items must be expensed here; payments to overseas service providers connected with these taxes must be subject to non-resident VAT and income tax withholding where chargeable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advertising, platform commissions to marketplaces, partner commissions, sales team payroll and freight or logistics related to customer acquisition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to a Taiwan sales agency may create permanent establishment exposure for the agency rather than the WFOE; for the WFOE, each commission must be supported by a signed agency agreement, service evidence and an arm's-length commission rate, otherwise the payment is disallowed and recharacterised as a divisible profit distribution subject to WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management, finance, HR, legal, R&D, office and IT administration expenses including director compensation, audit fees, and taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management-fee allocations from the Taiwan group are expressly non-deductible under Article 10 of the PRC EIT Law; shared-service and headquarters charges must be billed under a written cost-sharing arrangement with arm's-length mark-up and valid tendered invoices; qualifying R&D expenditures can claim the 100% super deduction, but only for activities physically performed in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on bank and related-party loans, guarantee fees, cash discounts and exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a Taiwan affiliate is limited by the 2:1 debt-to-equity safe-harbor ratio; the excess portion is non-deductible and may be treated as a deemed dividend; the deductible portion is subject to 10% statutory WHT on non-resident interest, reduced to 7% only if the Cross-Strait Agreement conditions are met and a valid tax residence certificate is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax after adding non-operating income and deducting non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line is the starting point for the tax reconciliation; all permanent and temporary differences for non-resident transactions (unreported WHT on deemed dividends, disallowed management fees, thin-capitalisation interest, transfer pricing adjustments) must be added back or removed through Schedules A105000/A105030/A105040/A105100 before computing taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 21 - Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: After Schedule A105000 adjustments, deductible losses and tax-incentive reductions, the final taxable income and tentative tax payable at the headline or preferential CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax at 25%, 15% or other applicable rate; offset foreign tax credits only for foreign-source income properly reported; if the WFOE is the withholding agent for dividends, interest or royalties to Taiwan, file the non-resident withholding declaration and pay the WHT separately from the CIT return, and ensure treaty relief has been administratively recognised before applying the reduced rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late quarterly or annual filing: up to RMB 10,000 fine under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law, with RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; late payment from the statutory due date: daily 0.05% surcharge under Article 32; understatement of taxable income by means of false or unsupported cross-border invoices: 50% to five times the unpaid tax under Article 63; wilful evasion may trigger criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment up to seven years; publication on the tax-dishonesty blacklist and joint punishment, including travel and exit restrictions for the responsible legal representative and directors, can follow.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding under Article 37 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law; reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement only for a Taiwan corporate beneficial owner that directly holds at least 25% of the paid-in capital of the Chinese WFOE and passes the beneficial-ownership and substance review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the dividend, interest or royalty payment date, the Taiwan recipient must (i) obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate from the competent Taiwan National Taxation Bureau; (ii) file the PRC application for tax-agreement treatment, with a beneficial-ownership declaration, with the competent PRC tax authority where the payer is registered; (iii) provide an organisational chart, audited financial statements, board minutes, evidence of actual premises, employees, decision-making and risk-bearing functions in Taiwan and, for dividends, shareholding registers proving 25% direct ownership; (iv) receive approval or record-filing before applying the reduced treaty rate. If approval is not obtained in time, the withholding agent must withhold at 10% and the Taiwan shareholder may claim a retrospective refund under the special adjustment procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on non-resident interest and royalties is 10% each under the PRC EIT Law. Under the Cross-Strait Agreement, interest and royalties payable to a Taiwan resident beneficial owner may be capped at 7% each, provided the recipient is the true owner, files the required residence certificate, and has no conduit arrangement with a third jurisdiction.
